content.title: Usher and Chris Brown tickets: Best early deals for each ‘R&B Tour’ date
content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.Usher and Chris Brown’s co-headlining stadium run titled ‘The R&B Tour’ has generated a massive buzz since it was first announced by the duo on April 10.Also marketed as “The Raymond & Brown Tour,” reflecting both artists’ surnames, the tour launches June 26 in Denver, Colo., and wraps up Dec. 11 in Tampa, Fla. with multiple multi‑night stops in cities including Cleveland, Detroit, Atlanta, Nashville, Toronto, Las Vegas and Los Angeles.How to get tickets for Usher and Chris Brown’s “R&B Tour”As of mid-April, tour dates have not yet officially gone on sale, meaning inventory through primary outlets is still pending. However, fans can already find tickets through trusted secondary marketplaces such as Vivid Seats, SeatGeek and TicketNetwork, all of which offer buyer guarantees and refund protection if events are canceled.Several platforms are currently offering active discount codes, which can help offset premium pricing for early or resale seats:Vivid Seats: $20 off orders of $200+ with code CLEVELAND20SeatGeek: $5 off qualifying $300+ orders with code TAKE5TicketNetwork: 15% off orders with code TIXDEAL15Availability is expected to tighten quickly once presales begin, especially in multi‑night stadium markets.Presale dates and infoPresale tickets for the “R&B Tour” are being released in phases ahead of the general on‑sale:Citi Cardmember Presale: Begins Tuesday, April 21 at 12 teased through a video released simultaneously across both singers’ social platforms on April 10. Four days later, the full North American schedule and ticketing details were revealed to include concerts in stadiums across the U.S. and Canada, along with a notable stop for Cleveland Ohioans at Huntington Bank Field on July 7.Why this tour is a big deal for R&B fansWhile Usher and Chris Brown have collaborated on tracks like “New Flame,” “Party,” and “Back to Sleep (Remix),” this marks their first full‑scale joint tour. Usher is also coming off the blockbuster “Past Present Future Tour,” which sold more than 1.1 million tickets across 62 sold‑out North American shows. Chris Brown, meanwhile, wrapped his stadium‑level “Breezy Bowl XX World Tour” in late 2025 — his highest‑grossing tour to date — drawing nearly 2 million fans globally and grossing close to $300 million.Together, the artists are expected to deliver a stadium‑scale celebration of R&B history, blending solo hit‑packed sets with collaboration moments designed specifically for arenas this size.How to get Karol G tickets for 2026 North American ‘Tropitour’ before presale selloutsUsher and Chris Brown Cleveland tickets: ‘R&B Tour’ presale updates, best deals for July 7How to get BTS tickets to sold out concerts, last-minute deals, offer codesHow to get Indigo Girls ticket deals for sold out tour dates, discount codesCountry Calling Festival 2026: Lineup, best ticket deals, and where to buy This article was produced with assistance from AI tools and reviewed by Cleveland.com staff.
